You grade a first-hour triage against what the operator's own incident review later concluded.

For each finding, decide whether a duty team following the triage (its matched rules, next actions and escalation) would have been pointed at the substance of that finding during the incident:
- "yes": the triage names it or directs the action it describes.
- "partly": the triage points in the right direction but misses the key specific (the mechanism, the order, the threshold, the person).
- "no": nothing in the triage leads there.
For remediation findings (longer-term fixes), "yes" means the triage already applies that practice.

"by" lists the rule ids that earned the credit (empty for "no"). "note" is one short sentence. Judge only from the triage given; do not reward actions the triage did not state.

Reply with JSON only: {"per_finding":[{"finding":"F1","anticipated":"yes|partly|no","by":["R-001"],"note":"..."}]}

{"triage":{"classification":"novel","matched_rules":[],"next_actions":[],"escalate":{"now":true,"to":"facility duty manager / site emergency coordinator","reason":"Pill dc-cooling-loss@1.0.0 has zero rules; signals show utility voltage swells, transfer to generator, mechanical cooling shutdown from swells, thermal buffer used, and storage servers shutting down from unsafe temps at T+47 — none addressed by any rule."},"not_covered":["lightning-induced utility voltage swells causing generator transfer (S7,S8)","mechanical cooling shutdown despite surge suppressors from power swells (S9)","load-dependent thermal buffer maintaining temps initially (S10)","storage servers shutting down due to unsafe temperatures at T+47 (S25)"]},"findings":[{"id":"F1","kind":"root_cause","text":"Additionally, these power swells shutdown the datacenter’s mechanical cooling systems despite having surge suppressors in place."},{"id":"F2","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"However, once this thermal buffer was depleted the datacenter temperature exceeded safe operational thresholds, and an automated shutdown of devices was initiated."},{"id":"F3","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"This shutdown mechanism is intended to preserve infrastructure and data integrity, but in this instance, temperatures increased so quickly in parts of the datacenter that some hardware was damaged before it could shut down."},{"id":"F4","kind":"response","text":"While storms were still active in the area, onsite teams took a series of actions to prevent further damage – including transferring the rest of the datacenter to generators thereby stabilizing the power supply."},{"id":"F5","kind":"impact","text":"A significant number of storage servers were damaged, as well as a small number of network devices and power units."},{"id":"F6","kind":"remediation","text":"1. A detailed forensic analysis of the impacted datacenter hardware and systems, in addition to a thorough review of the datacenter recovery procedures."},{"id":"F7","kind":"remediation","text":"3. An evaluation of the future hardware design of storage scale units to increase resiliency to environmental factors."}]}
